row.text: The Quapaw Bathhouse took its name from Native American artifacts found when its basement was dug.
The Quapaw's dome tower is the highest on Bathhouse Row and is topped with a copper cupola.
The National Park Service says the Quapaw is one of two places where visitors can soak in the thermal springs.
The Hale, built in 1892-93 to replace an earlier bathhouse, is the oldest surviving bathhouse on the Row.
After the Lamar closed in 1985, the Buckstaff was the only bathhouse still operating on the Row.

bridge.text: The first World's Shortest St. Patrick's Day Parade marched down Bridge Street on March 17, 2004, drawing more than 2,000 people.
bridge.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: World's Shortest St. Patrick's Day Parade

bridge.text: By 2016 the fire marshal estimated the Bridge Street parade crowd at nearly 30,000 people.
bridge.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: World's Shortest St. Patrick's Day Parade

bridge.text: Bridge Street was written up in Ripley's Believe It or Not as the world's shortest street in everyday use.
bridge.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: World's Shortest St. Patrick's Day Parade

bridge.text: A group of 100 marching "Irish" Elvis Presley impersonators once took part in the parade.
bridge.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: World's Shortest St. Patrick's Day Parade

bridge.text: The Malco Theatre, rebuilt after a Christmas Eve 1935 fire, stands on the site of the Princess Theatre, where Bridge Street meets Central Avenue and Broadway.

central.text: The second Arlington Hotel burned to the ground on April 5, 1923, and the current third hotel replaced it.
The Arlington says Al Capone was a frequent guest in the 1930s and rented an entire floor for his entourage.
In 1928 Senator Joe T. Robinson announced his acceptance of the Democratic vice-presidential nomination, broadcast by KTHS, the radio station based at the Arlington.
The Southern Club, the private club of Charles Dugan and Dan Stuart, opened in 1893 at 250 Central Avenue and now houses a wax museum.
The Ohio Club, founded in 1905 at 336 Central Avenue, is considered Arkansas's oldest continually operating bar.

oaklawn.text: By 1914 Oaklawn was owned by brothers Louis A. and Charles Cella of St. Louis.
oaklawn.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Oaklawn Park Racetrack

oaklawn.text: The first Arkansas Derby ran in 1936 with a purse of $5,000.
oaklawn.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Oaklawn Park Racetrack

oaklawn.text: A state law passed February 27, 1907, banning betting on horse races forced Oaklawn to close after the 1907 season.
oaklawn.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Oaklawn Park Racetrack

oaklawn.text: In 2005 Oaklawn and the Cella family received an Eclipse Award of Merit.
oaklawn.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Oaklawn Park Racetrack

lakes.text: Blakely Mountain Dam is 231 feet tall and 1,100 feet long, and cost $31 million.
lakes.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Blakely Mountain Dam

lakes.text: The dam's power plant began generating electricity on July 17, 1955, and the dam was dedicated on July 4, 1956.
lakes.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Blakely Mountain Dam

lakes.text: Lake Ouachita covers over 40,000 acres and is the largest lake entirely within Arkansas.
lakes.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Blakely Mountain Dam

lakes.text: Garvan Woodland Gardens is a 210-acre botanical garden on four and a half miles of Lake Hamilton shoreline.
lakes.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Garvan Woodland Gardens

lakes.text: Lake Hamilton was created when Arkansas Power and Light built Carpenter Dam, which left the Garvan land as a large peninsula.
lakes.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Garvan Woodland Gardens

ballfields.text: Babe Ruth trained at Hot Springs many times and became a very familiar face around town.
ballfields.source: Hot Springs Baseball Trail: Whittington Park

ballfields.text: Bill Dickey was discovered in Hot Springs while substituting for a friend in a semi-pro game at Whittington Park.
ballfields.source: Hot Springs Baseball Trail: Whittington Park

ballfields.text: Fogel Field, also known as Fordyce Field, was built in 1912 by the Hot Springs Park Company.
ballfields.source: Hot Springs Baseball Trail: See the Trail

ballfields.text: The Baseball Trail says more baseball was played at the Whittington Park corner than anywhere else in Hot Springs.
ballfields.source: Hot Springs Baseball Trail: Whittington Park

ballfields.text: The Baseball Trail says no player left a bigger legacy in Hot Springs than Honus Wagner, 'the Flying Dutchman.'
ballfields.source: Hot Springs Baseball Trail: Whittington Park

hollow.text: Photographer Norman McLeod came to Hot Springs in 1888, and Happy Hollow began as his picture studio.
Visitors posed for pictures in an old bathtub, on a burro, or taking a drink at the bar.
The park had a shooting gallery, a zoo and a souvenir shop.
Happy Hollow stood at the head of Fountain Street, just off Central Avenue.
The Encyclopedia of Arkansas says all that remains of Happy Hollow are its springs on the southeast slope of North Mountain.

park.text: Bill Clinton lived at 1011 Park Avenue as a child, from 1954 to 1961; the home is not open for tours.
park.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Bill Clinton Boyhood Home

park.text: The Arkansas Historic Preservation Program calls the Clinton boyhood home the area's finest example of Tudor Revival style.
park.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Bill Clinton Boyhood Home

park.text: The 1925 paved highway from Little Rock became Park Avenue as it entered Hot Springs.
park.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Mountainaire Hotel Historic District

park.text: The Mountainaire's Art Moderne buildings on Park Avenue were built in 1947 by Alvin Albinson, who came from Florida for the tourist trade.
park.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Mountainaire Hotel Historic District

park.text: The Velda Rose Tower Motor Hotel, an International Style hotel, was among the Arkansas additions to the National Register of Historic Places announced in 2024.

trivia.grandJury: In 1946 a federal judge threw out almost a quarter of the poll tax receipts used in the primary, after GI reform candidates sued.

hs-0256.question: What length of basketball shot clock did the Arkansas Activities Association vote in 2020 to make mandatory for all member schools?
hs-0256.questionWas: How long is the shot clock in Arkansas high school basketball, as used by Hot Springs teams?
hs-0256.explanation: The 2020 resolution made the 35-second shot clock mandatory for every school by the 2022-23 school year.
hs-0256.explanationWas: A resolution making the 35-second shot clock mandatory for all schools by 2022-23 passed in 2020.

hs-0264.question: Which Arkansas Derby winner went on to win the 1983 Kentucky Derby?
hs-0264.questionWas: How many Kentucky Derby winners had the Arkansas Derby produced, per a Visit Hot Springs article?
hs-0264.explanation: Visit Hot Springs lists Sunny's Halo (1983) first among eight Arkansas Derby winners that took the Kentucky Derby; Lil E. Tee, Grindstone and Super Saver on the same list won in 1992, 1996 and 2010.
hs-0264.explanationWas: The article lists winners from Sunny's Halo (1983) through Mystik Dan (2024).

hs-0367.explanation: Visit Hot Springs describes Art Springs as a free, two-day art festival and showcase within its Arts & the Park celebration; a 2026 listing shows it again that spring.
hs-0367.explanationWas: Visit Hot Springs calls it a free, two-day art festival and showcase; it listed Arts & the Park as April 24 to May 3 in 2020.

hs-0383.explanation: Organizers cited an abundance of caution over COVID-19 when moving the races; a 2026 Visit Hot Springs release says no races were held in 2020.
hs-0383.explanationWas: Organizers cited "an abundance of caution" over the COVID-19 pandemic when moving the races.

hs-0386.question: Which race at Hot Springs' Güdrun mountain bike festival is named for a famous conqueror?
hs-0386.questionWas: Which race at Hot Springs' Güdrun Mountain Biking Festival is named for a famous conqueror?
hs-0386.explanation: Visit Hot Springs described the Güdrun festival in 2020 as including the annual Attila the Hun Mountain Bike Race; the 2026 festival, now billed as the Güdrun - Northwoods MTB Festival, still lists an Attila the Hun XC race.
hs-0386.explanationWas: The Güdrun Mountain Biking Festival (Nov. 13-15 in the 2020 listing) includes the annual Attila the Hun Mountain Bike Race.

hs-0388.explanation: The Spa Running Festival is a November race weekend in Hot Springs with a Summit2Summit half marathon, a 10K, a 5K and a children's Squirt Race; the race's own page describes the course as running through Hot Springs National Park.
hs-0388.explanationWas: The 2020 listing (Nov. 13-15) also included a 10K, a 5K and a 1K for children.

hs-0390.explanation: A 2020 Visit Hot Springs listing said Brian Martin and Blues Traveler would play on Monday, March 16, and Foghat on Tuesday, following the parade.
hs-0390.explanationWas: Blues Traveler was announced for Monday, March 16, the day before the parade.

hs-0396.explanation: The festival's own site says it brings over 100 international musicians to Hot Springs each June for two weeks of concerts and open rehearsals.
hs-0396.explanationWas: Visit Hot Springs listed the 2020 festival as May 31 to June 13.

hs-0432.question: On what date did Magic Springs reopen after its mid-1990s closure?
hs-0432.questionWas: On what date did Magic Springs reopen after its late-1990s closure?
hs-0432.explanation: Wikipedia says the park closed in 1995 and that Magic Springs and Crystal Falls reopened on May 27, 2000, after Hot Springs voters approved a bond issue.
hs-0432.explanationWas: Magic Springs and Crystal Falls reopened on May 27, 2000, after voters approved a bond issue.

hs-0442.explanation: Magic Springs' website said the 2025 season marked the official retirement of the wooden coaster, which it said would stay permanently closed; the park said it would not remove the ride for the foreseeable future.
hs-0442.explanationWas: Magic Springs said the 2025 season marked its official retirement; the coaster remains standing but not operating.

hs-0459.explanation: The festival's own site says its two weeks include over 20 concerts and 250 open rehearsals.
hs-0459.explanationWas: Visit Hot Springs lists over 20 concerts and over 250 open rehearsals for the festival's May 31-June 13, 2020 run.

hs-0460.question: In what year was Hot Springs' Valley of the Vapors Independent Music Festival first held?
hs-0460.questionWas: Which March indie music festival in Hot Springs brings 140-plus musicians to small venue stages?
hs-0460.explanation: The festival was started by Bill Solleder and Shea Childs, who formed the nonprofit Low Key Arts to run it.
hs-0460.explanationWas: The 2020 Valley of the Vapors Independent Music Festival (March 20-23) planned 140-plus musicians on small venue stages.

hs-0464.question: Which film spent a week shooting at Hot Springs' Malco Theatre during production in 2023?
hs-0464.questionWas: Which 2023 film spent a week shooting at Hot Springs' Malco Theatre?
hs-0464.explanation: The Sentinel-Record reported in June 2023 that much of the film was shot in downtown Hot Springs, including a week at the Malco Theatre.
hs-0464.explanationWas: The Sentinel-Record says much of the film was shot in downtown Hot Springs, including a week at the Malco Theatre.

hs-0465.explanation: The Sentinel-Record reported in March 2022 that Little Rock native Joey Lauren Adams was directing the television movie, titled Betrayed Within on a city permit application, which was filmed in part at the Arlington Resort Hotel & Spa.
hs-0465.explanationWas: The article says Visit Hot Springs' Bill Solleder, the film commissioner, issues film permits.

hs-0466.question: In what year did Hot Springs' Spa-Con comics and pop culture convention begin?
hs-0466.questionWas: Which comic and pop-culture convention was listed for September 18-20, 2020 in Hot Springs?
hs-0466.explanation: The name plays on Hot Springs' nickname, the Spa City, and the convention is generally held at the Hot Springs Convention Center.
hs-0466.explanationWas: The 2020 listing (Sept. 18-20) named guests including actress Lori Petty and Rodger Bumpass, the voice of Squidward.
